descriptionChirho: Describing a state of readiness or preparedness, whether of persons who are poised for action or of things that have been made ready. Arabic 'مُسْتَعِدِّينَ/مُسْتَعِدٍّ' (mustaʿiddīn, ready/prepared) and 'مَا سَيَأْتِيهِمْ' (what will come to them), Korean '준비된' (junbidoen, prepared), Spanish 'preparados/preparado/lo preparado' (prepared/the prepared things), Hindi 'तैयार/आनेवाली बातें' (taiyār, ready / ānevālī bātẽ, coming things), Swahili 'tayari/mambo yaliyoandaliwa' (ready/things prepared) — five occurrences sharing the core notion of readiness.

A ketiv (written) reading that diverges from the qere, apparently denoting stored wealth or treasures rather than 'readiness.' Hindi 'खजानों' (khazānõ, treasures) and Swahili 'hazina zao' (their treasure) point to a distinct lexical referent of accumulated riches or storehouses, distinguishing this single occurrence from the standard adjectival sense of preparedness found elsewhere in the lemma's distribution.
